transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand very quiet at the edge of my father's domain. Most who fall here are screaming, or begging for a rope back to the sun. Why are you silent?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm looking for my brother Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The one with the loud voice. He is deep in the tunnels by now, likely forgetting his own name. Do you think you can pull him back from that?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't think I can.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you waste my time. You came for a ghost? If you believe he is gone, you should have stayed in the sun and mourned him there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I couldn't stay up there.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you came down to die with him. That is not brave, little one. That is simply giving up in a different direction.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not trying to be brave.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You confuse me. You do not plead, you do not weep, and you do not fight. You only stand there and tell me he is lost.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's my brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: And what good is a brother who cannot answer you? What good is a husk? You are chasing smoke.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I still have to find him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Find him to do what? Watch his eyes slide through you as if you are only air? That is a precise kind of torture you are choosing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just need to see him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are stubborn in a dull way. Humans usually bargain immediately; they offer limbs, years, secrets, anything to change the ending.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't have any secrets.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have the moment he fell. I can smell the guilt on you like old sweat. Did you push him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him to yell at the well.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ah. And now you think walking into the beast’s mouth will make it spit him back out. That is not acceptance. That is a transaction you still hope will work.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know it won't spit him out.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you are a fool who walks toward pain with his eyes open. Why not stay above and let forgetting do its work—just as it will surely work on him?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I couldn't sleep while he was down here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Sleep is for the living. You speak like you are already dead. Where is the fire? Where is the screaming?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm done screaming.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A pity. Echoes are the only entertainment this place offers. If you are empty of fear and empty of hope, what moves your legs?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I promised I'd be right behind him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A promise to the air? He cannot hear you, and he cannot hold you to it. Who is this promise for?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: For me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Selfishness. That sits better on you than nobility. You came to scrub your conscience clean, to rinse the dare off your hands.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't think it comes off.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you are trapped. You cannot save him, and you cannot forgive yourself. Why cross my gate if the heavy things will cross with you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because being up there feels wrong.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Wrong how? The sun is warm, the dates are sweet, and the ground is solid. Why does the surface feel wrong to a boy who belongs in light?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because he isn't there.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you throw away the whole world because it is missing one loud piece. That sounds like a child's tantrum, not resolve.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not trying to resolve anything. I just want to pass.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Pass into what? You admit you cannot save him, and you admit you cannot wash the guilt away. You are walking into fire simply because you cannot tolerate the cold.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It's not about being tired.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then explain it so a monster can understand. I have seen men weep for gold and mothers weep for sons, but they all wanted something returned. You want nothing back. Why are you here?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because he shouldn't be down here alone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Alone is how everyone ends, little shadow. You think your presence will comfort a boy who may not remember his own face? You bring water to a drowning man.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'd rather drown with him than stay dry up there.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is. You value your own safety less than a corpse’s comfort. Hope is not driving you—only the inability to stand still.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I couldn't stand still anymore.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you came because the alternative was unbearable. Not to win. Not to save. Just because you could not endure the other path. That is a dangerous kind of motion.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't feel free.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are, though. Men with hope are easy to steer because they fear losing it. You have nothing left to lose, so you simply walk.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I walk through the gate?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You ask permission like a guest, yet you stand there like a ghost. I have crushed kings who demanded entry, but my hands stay at my sides. It is exhausting to threaten someone who does not care if he lives or dies.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I care. I just care about him more.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is that small sharp thing again—that loyalty that smells like blood. It is the only part of you that feels solid; the rest is already halfway swallowed. Perhaps there is no point guarding the dark from a shadow.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Does that mean you'll move?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: It means the stone is tired of your stubborn silence. Do you hear the chains retracting in the walls? They are not used to opening for a boy with nothing in his pockets.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hear them.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are a strange anomaly—walking into fire because you cannot bear the cold. The mechanism yields not to your strength, but to your absolute lack of it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then stop waiting for me to change my mind. The way is open, and the black air is already reaching for your throat. Go, before I remember what I am.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not thank me for letting you drown. The gate stands wide now, a mouth that does not close behind you. Run to your brother, little fool.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm coming, Omar.
